$comment: COPY THIS, then delete every $comment. Files beginning with '_' are skipped by
`tcat-validate all`, which is why this template can carry comments and REPLACE
placeholders. Your copy must not start with '_'.
A sample document is authored by the lab that MADE the sample, once. Every
dataset measured on it then carries only `sample_id`. Repeating synthesis
history on each dataset guarantees the copies diverge, and then nobody knows
The `properties` object is the part worth planning for. Correlating a fitted
rate constant against an independently measured catalyst property is a JOIN
between a fit and the properties recorded here. If those live in a notebook,
that comparison becomes a spreadsheet exercise at the worst possible moment.
$comment_id: Verbatim what is written on the vial. A project-assigned relabelling scheme
that disagrees with the physical label is a scheme that gets ignored.
$comment_status: Flag, never delete -- this applies to samples too. A synthesis that failed, or
a sample that was contaminated, is retained with a status_reason. Those are
often the most informative entries in a materials series.
$comment_composition: Both, where both exist -- the difference between what was intended and what
was made is frequently the interesting variable. A MEASURED composition must
name its method; a composition without one is not comparable across labs.
$comment_synthesis: thermal_treatments is ORDERED: calcination-then-reduction is a different
Record the precursor `lot`. A precursor lot change is a classic culprit for
unexplained drift between nominally identical samples, and it is unrecoverable
$comment_properties: Every entry needs value + units + method. `dataset_ref` makes the value
auditable rather than asserted -- point it at the characterization dataset it
Use "1" for a genuinely dimensionless quantity. Never omit units.

characterization.summary: REPLACE -- one line of what it showed.

$comment_batch: Datasets inherit batch_id from the sample they measure, and that inheritance
is what makes grouped train/test splits correct rather than approximate.
Same-batch data must stay within one split.
$comment_parent: For a sample derived from another -- a split batch, a re-calcined portion, a
spent sample recovered after reaction. Makes the materials lineage explicit
instead of implied by a naming convention.
notes: REPLACE. Storage conditions, anything anomalous about the synthesis, why a sample was abandoned. The validator warns when this is empty.

extensions.$comment: Your escape hatch. The validator ignores this rather than rejecting it.
